purpose: Classroom locator maps for Volume I, chapters III–IV, with selected geographic contexts; not a navigation product or complete itinerary.
crs: WGS84 longitude/latitude in GeoJSON; Leaflet projects to Web Mercator. map-config.json fields are named lat and lon.

geometry.processing: Individual whole polygons intersecting longitude -100 to 30 and latitude 0 to 75 retained without simplifying or clipping their coordinates. Includes Canada, Greenland, Iceland and northern Europe, absent from the chapters 1–2 regional subset. Modern borders are orientation only.

geometry.transformation: Individual whole polygons intersecting longitude -18 to 30 and latitude 25 to 65 retained with original coordinates, plus Barbados. This generous regional margin supplies all surrounding land in the Channel, Mediterranean and Thames views across desktop/mobile aspect ratios. Properties reduced to NAME and ADM0_A3.
geometry.use: Island and coastal detail; modern boundaries, not eighteenth-century jurisdictions

geometry.transformation: One feature selected by name Thames; original coordinates retained.
geometry.use: Generalized Thames centerline for classroom orientation. Line ends near Gravesend; no exact lower-river anchorage or 1762 shoreline reconstructed.

movement: No route lines or battle positions. Selected named places and a broad Virginia regional label. Narrative sequence appears in prose. Sea calls, islands and areas are not represented as equally precise coordinates.
limits: Chapters include repeated voyages and additional calls; this is not a complete itinerary.
Barbados is a transfer point; the text specifies Equiano was not sold there.
Virginia river and plantation are unnamed and are not pinned.
First English arrival date is not independently asserted here.
Cape Logas belongs to the Portuguese battle episode; the Lagos marker is contextual.
Deptford is the beginning of forced boat transfer. Sale occurs aboard a ship below Gravesend; that anchorage is not pinned.
Thames geometry is generalized modern vector data, not a street-level, hydrographic or reconstructed eighteenth-century map.
No new PDF produced. Static SVG maps and an accessible place list provide fallback.

qa.place_coordinates: All named locators fall within configured view bounds. Guernsey, Belle-Île, Falmouth, Barcelona and Lagos checked against their Natural Earth country/island polygons. Toulon uses the harbour vicinity.
qa.static: Four real-geometry SVG fallbacks generated from the same configuration; each uses sans-serif font and an approximate scale at map centre.
qa.contextual_land: The 10m regional dataset includes Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Italy, Sardinia, Ireland, and neighboring countries. View data is selected by a generous geographic bounding box, not by the narrative place list.
